extraction.name: VoiceAssistant-Eval
extraction.description: A benchmark of 10,497 curated question-answer examples across 13 task categories for evaluating voice-first AI assistants' listening, speaking, and viewing capabilities. It includes natural sounds, music, speech, multi-round dialogue, emotion, instruction following, reasoning, robustness, role-play voice imitation, safety, and image-based multidisciplinary understanding.
extraction.creator: Ke Wang; Houxing Ren; Zimu Lu; Mingjie Zhan; Hongsheng Li
extraction.inLanguage: English; Chinese. Five role-play roles are Chinese; all other prompts and evaluations are in English.
extraction.citeAs: Ke Wang, Houxing Ren, Zimu Lu, Mingjie Zhan, and Hongsheng Li. VoiceAssistant-Eval: Benchmarking AI Assistants Across Listening, Speaking, and Viewing. arXiv:2509.22651v1, 26 September 2025.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The authors collect questions, reference answers, metadata, audio, and images from existing datasets, convert text instructions into spoken prompts, and apply manual and automated curation. Listening inputs come from 23 audio-understanding datasets; speaking tasks use RoleBench and other text and audio datasets; viewing inputs come from MMMU. For voice personalization, 100 distinct roles are selected with three representative audio clips per role. Deduplication, validation, categorization into 13 tasks, and sampling produce 10,497 final examples. Table 2 reports 47 source datasets, whereas the introduction states 37.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis; Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Candidate items with missing or broken audio or images, corrupted images, or silent audio are excluded. Approximately 10% of candidates are discarded during validation, which also removes ill-posed prompts and incorrect answers; the paper does not separately quantify missing-media cases.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Existing academic datasets supply raw prompts, reference answers, metadata, audio waveforms, images, and optional multi-turn transcripts. Sources include RoleBench for role profiles and questions, MMMU for multidisciplinary images and questions, and speech, sound, music, dialogue, reasoning, instruction-following, and safety datasets listed in Table 8. MMMU spans 30 disciplines and 30 image formats. Three representative role audio clips are collected for each of 100 roles.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Text questions are rewritten using Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct for speech synthesis. Image tokens are replaced with descriptive phrases, mathematical expressions and numbers are converted into pronounceable forms, and multiple-choice options are rephrased. F5-TTS, ChatTTS, and Dia-1.6B synthesize spoken questions using 300 role audio clips as prompts to increase speaker diversity. Generated speech is regenerated until its UTMOS Strong score exceeds 3.8, then transcribed with Whisper-Large-v3; the sample with the lowest word error rate is selected. The authors synthesize 13,471 speech audio files.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Lexical overlap and Levenshtein distance flag potential duplicate questions, which are manually reviewed and removed, leaving 15,359 samples. Curators then check media integrity, task well-posedness, answer validity, and multi-turn coherence. Missing, corrupted, silent, incomplete, ambiguous, unsuitable, or incorrectly answered items are excluded. Remaining items are assigned to 13 task categories primarily using source metadata and sampled to balance task ratios. Approved items are exported to clean JSONL shards, yielding 10,497 examples.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Curators review candidate prompts, reference answers, metadata, media, transcripts, and multiple-choice options, assigning a Good or Bad quality verdict and optional notes. Review checks media integrity, prompt clarity and alignment, reference-answer validity, and multi-turn coherence. Task categories are assigned primarily from source metadata. Separately, human judges independently evaluate 1,050 sampled Qwen2.5-Omni-7B responses to validate automated evaluation, and the authors manually examine 593 error cases for qualitative error analysis.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: A custom lightweight web-based curation tool with a single-screen interface, inline audio players and image viewers, transcripts, multiple-choice options, reference answers, Good/Bad verdict controls, and optional notes. It exports audit logs containing item IDs, curator decisions, and timestamps.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Approved curation items are retained in clean JSONL shards, while rejected items are discarded. For validation of model-response ratings, human judges independently assess 1,050 responses sampled across all 13 tasks. Agreement between gpt-oss-20b and human evaluation is measured using Pearson correlation and agreement rate, yielding overall values of 0.92 and 96.1%, respectively. The paper does not describe a procedure for resolving disagreements among human annotators.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: gpt-oss-20b generates task-specific quality judgments for model responses. emotion2vec supplies probabilities for angry, disgusted, fearful, happy, neutral, sad, and surprised emotions, retaining probabilities above 1% in evaluator prompts. Whisper-Large-v3 generates speech transcriptions. These tools support automated evaluation and speech validation rather than a stated process for authoring new human reference answers.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset and reproduction code will be publicly released. The authors will maintain a data-governance process for auditing and removal and reserve the right to update assets if consent or licensing concerns arise. No update schedule, versioning policy, or deprecation timeframe is specified.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The benchmark includes speaker voice recordings and role voice profiles used for voice imitation and speaker-similarity evaluation. Examples contain speaker gender labels, spoken-language labels, age descriptions, and emotion labels. The authors explicitly discuss consent and privacy concerns associated with reproducing identifiable speakers.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark aims to support trustworthy, reliable voice assistants, including hands-free applications in safety-critical and accessibility-oriented settings. Role-play voice imitation creates risks of identity spoofing, harassment, fraud, impersonation, privacy violations, and unequal performance across demographics. The authors require consent and provenance safeguards, consent gating, watermarking or traceability of synthetic audio, and safety cards describing acceptable use, known risks, and voice-cloning red-team tests.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The benchmark may inherit biases from source datasets and design choices. Academic and synthetic questions, including rewritten instructions, may not reflect real deployment contexts or fairness concerns. The fixed set of 100 role-play roles and style prompts may encode stereotypes or omit important user personas. Its predominantly English prompts limit linguistic diversity. Automated GPT-based evaluation may favor particular phrasings, overlook nuanced errors, and fail to capture all human preferences.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The 10.5K-item dataset may have limited diversity and may not generalize to diverse linguistic settings because all prompts and evaluations except five Chinese roles are English. Academic and synthetic sources limit realism. Video-audio integration and continuous audiovisual streaming are outside scope. Evaluation is offline and static and does not measure latency, partial-utterance handling, user interruption, or error recovery. Automated metrics and GPT-based judgments may introduce noise and bias. The reported model comparison includes only one proprietary system because of cost and access constraints.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Intended for testing and benchmarking voice assistants across listening, speaking, and viewing, assessing response content, speech quality, consistency, voice imitation, robustness, and safety, and tracking progress toward improved multimodal assistants. The dataset is not intended for training models to cheat on the benchmark. Training or releasing models intended to reproduce identifiable speakers without documented consent is prohibited. Downstream users must implement consent gating and watermarking or traceability of synthetic audio. The authors encourage analysis of biased or unsafe outputs and contributions of additional fairness and ethics test cases.
